content_units: Weekend Watchlist for Two

A balanced weekend lineup from your catalog is straightforward: pick one sharper thriller, one easy-reset comedy, one high-upside documentary, and one flexible backup that still fits the time cap. All selected titles are   under 2h 20m   and   avoid horror  .
Ranked Picks and Why They Fit
Option 1:   Glass Harbor     Smart weekend anchor for your thriller slot     118 min, rating 8.1
- Best match for the “smart thriller” request because it pairs a strong rating with a tense, likely conversation-friendly vibe.
- At just under 2 hours, it feels substantial without becoming a late-night commitment.
- Better fit than  Moonlit Heist  if you want something more cerebral than stylish.
Option 2:   Late Checkout     Best light-comedy pick for keeping the weekend breezy     96 min, rating 7.2
- “Witty” is the strongest direct match for a couple wanting a lighter counterbalance to a thriller.
- Short runtime makes it ideal after dinner or as a low-effort second feature.
- Chosen over  Family Recipe  because “light comedy” usually benefits more from sharp pacing than warmth.
Option 3:   Tiny Planets     Easiest documentary recommendation in the catalog     88 min, rating 8.5
- Highest-rated title in the whole set and the only documentary, so it cleanly fills that slot.
- The “awe” mood makes it perfect between heavier narrative picks.
- At 88 minutes, it adds variety without tiring the weekend schedule.
Option 4:   Family Recipe     Safest backup if you want something softer and more affectionate     104 min, rating 7.6
- Good fallback if the couple wants a more comforting tone than the thriller or witty comedy.
- “Warm” makes it especially useful if you want a Sunday-night palate cleanser.
- Better backup than  Ashes of Winter  because the latter sounds emotionally heavy, and better than  Deep Signal  if you want lower intensity.
Best Viewing Order for the Weekend
Saturday night — Glass Harbor
- Start with the smartest, most engaging pick when attention is highest.
- Its tense tone makes it the best “main event” watch.
Later Saturday or Sunday afternoon — Late Checkout
- Use this as the release valve after the thriller.
- The shorter runtime keeps the weekend feeling relaxed.
Sunday evening — Tiny Planets
- Ends the weekend on a high-quality, expansive note.
- “Awe” is a better closing mood than something heavy or bleak.
If one title doesn’t fit the mood — Family Recipe
- Swap it in for either the comedy slot or the Sunday slot.
- Most flexible backup because it stays light and couple-friendly.
Selection Logic
What was filtered out
-   Street of Echoes   — excluded because it’s   horror

- No runtime exclusions were needed because every non-horror title is   140 minutes or less  , except  Ashes of Winter  at 141 minutes, which is still within your max of 140? Actually,   2h 20m = 140 minutes  , so  Ashes of Winter  is   over limit   and excluded.
Why these four rose to the top
-   Genre match first:   thriller, comedy, documentary, backup
-   Mood balance second:   tense + witty + awe + warm creates a strong weekend flow
-   Runtime third:   all picks are easy to slot into a couple’s weekend
-   Ratings as tiebreaker:   helped choose  Glass Harbor  over  Moonlit Heist , and  Late Checkout  over a softer but less directly “light” alternative

Catalog Notes
Using your catalog as provided, I treated   “smart thriller”   as favoring the stronger-rated, more serious thriller and   “light comedy”   as favoring the brisker, witty option over the warmer one.
